body:
As hinted at by @rburing this isn't the case, so we might as well omit this.

You can see this not being true with a simple test: [get-rest-info-motion.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19669174/get-rest-info-motion.zip)

Zero out the `motion` property on the `ShapeQuery` node in that test and you'll see that the results of the query changes.

This is just from a quick glance, but as best I can tell, the motion vector is incorporated to achieve something similar to what's done for `cast_motion` and `body_test_motion` in 3D, with its `GodotMotionShape3D`, where the calculated support is elongated by the motion vector to effectively stretch the query shape.

What the exact use-case for this is supposed to be, or why there is a discrepancy between 2D and 3D, I have no idea, unfortunately.
